Cc: procure@crosswind.ai

Subject: Crosswind evaluation — subsidy ask + safety gating

Hi Vivek / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Crosswind is running a comparative bakeoff next month and we want to make sure we have a close apples-to-apples run against Redwood and two other vendors. Procurement asked me to consolidate subsidy offers and also confirm any guardrails you can put in place around data handling and output safety during the eval.

Can you confirm:
- The maximum trial credit/top-up you can provide for a 2-week bakeoff (we typically run ~300k tokens total per model)
- Whether you can commit to audit logs and a short-term SOC2 evidence packet for this eval window
- Any constraints around model prompt sampling or rate limits during the test

I've attached the RFP summary (crosswind-rfp-summary.pdf). Timeline: we need firm numbers and procurement-ready language by Thu 22 Apr so we can include it in the commercial comparison.

Thanks — appreciate a quick sketch that I can pass to our sourcing team.

—Ana
Ana Ruiz
Head of Product
Crosswind AI

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Ana Ruiz <ana@crosswind.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Crosswind evaluation — subsidy ask + safety gating

Ana — thanks for the clear ask and the RFP. High level answer up front: we can support a tailored subsidy + short-term compliance artifacts for the bakeoff. Details below so procurement has something to use.

Proposed offer (draft):
- Baseline eval credit: 50,000 token-credit package (usable across our hosted endpoints)
- Performance top-up: up to an additional 100,000 tokens contingent on participation in a short eval questionnaire and sharing anonymized prompts/results for aggregate QA
- One-time private trial option: if Crosswind wants to run a VPC-for-eval (private deployment), we can provide a 2-week Private trial with the baseline credits applied; private trial scope requires an NDA and platform access request form.

Security & compliance commitments:
- Audit logs: yes, we can provide request/response logs for the bakeoff window with redaction options for PII
- SOC2 evidence: we can provide a short evidence packet (in-scope controls and recent test report excerpt) suitable for procurement review; full reporting requires standard intake but we can fast-track a readout for the two-week window

Operational notes / limits:
- Rate limits: 100 rps default for the hosted eval package; can be temporarily increased for the private trial
- Sampling/randomness: we will not change model sampling behavior for the bakeoff; any deterministic runs should be coordinated so results are comparable

Next steps we need from you:
1) Confirm which option you prefer (hosted eval with credits vs Private trial)
2) Procurement contact + PO timing (we can put a short commercial note into DocuSign once you confirm)

I've attached a proposed-subsidy-model.xlsx with the token buckets and optional top-up mechanics. Ben / Karthik — tagging you for pricing and private trial feasibility. Marissa — can you confirm authorization range for the top-up (we typically require manager approval for >75k token supplements).

Thanks,
Vivek
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Crosswind evaluation — subsidy ask + safety gating

Vivek — this is very helpful. A couple of quick clarifications from procurement and legal: 

1) For the audit logs, we need assurance that logs will include timestamps, full request payloads, and model-generated tokens (redacted where PII is detected). Can Redwood provide a sample log extract?
2) For SOC2, we don't need the entire report in advance; a one-page control summary + attestation is sufficient for our sourcing team. Can you agree to share that by Thu 22 Apr?
3) IP/data handling: will any user-provided prompts or outputs be stored and used to further train models? Crosswind requires an opt-out for training for the bakeoff period.

If you can confirm the above and move the baseline to 75k tokens (given the cross-model runs), we are likely to mark Redwood as 'preferred' for scoring.

On timing: procurement will aim to issue a PO by Mon 26 Apr.

Thanks,
Ana

Ana — quick follow-up on the technical asks. Short answers below and then a proposed procurement-ready clause.

- Sample log extract: yes — attached are redacted examples (we can provide a narrowed sample showing timestamp, request body, and generated token stream).
- Training opt-out: for the hosted eval we can agree to an explicit no-training flag for the bakeoff window; for Private trial, no customer data leaves the VPC and nothing is used to train our public models.
- SOC2 one-pager: we will provide a control summary + contact for our compliance team by end of day Thu 22 Apr.

Procurement clause (draft you can paste into the RFP):
"Redwood Inference agrees to provide Crosswind AI with a 75,000 token evaluation credit package, plus consideration of an additional 50,000 token top-up contingent on returning an evaluation questionnaire and sharing anonymized output logs. Redwood will provide redacted audit logs (timestamps, request/response pairs, token streams) for the evaluation window and will not use customer-supplied prompts or outputs to train public models during the bakeoff period. SOC2 control summary and compliance contact will be delivered by 2027-04-22."

Ben — Marissa — request your sign-off if this fits within the authorization envelope for credits/top-ups. We can convert the clause into a short DocuSign addendum once we have Marissa's approval.
